newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Private transfers to Israel rose one pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Private transfers to Israel rose one pct in 1996.

text.p: Net unilateral transfers to Israel in the private sector barely grew last year after rising sharply in 1994 and 1995, the Bank of Israel said on Wednesday.
The central bank said net private sector transfers to Israel reached $4.32 billion last year, a rise of one percent. In 1995 private sector transfers grew 14 percent and in 1994 by 20 percent.

As a result, private sector transfers covered only 47 percent of Israel's goods and services trade deficit, down from 70 percent in 1993. The trade deficit widened 7.7 percent last year to $9.14 billion.
"Unilateral transfers constitute, as is known, the major component for financing the deficit in the goods and service accounts of the balance of payments," the bank said.
Israel is also the recipient of government transfers mainly from $3 billion annually in U.S. foreign aid.

The central bank attributed last year's small rise in net unilateral transfers to slowing immigration from the former Soviet Union. Transfers by immigrants had been responsible for most of the sharp rises of the previous two years.
Some 69,000 immigrants arrived in Israel last year, down from 79,000, according to the Central Bureau of Statistics.
The bank said unilateral transfers out of the country, much of it by Israelis living abroad, increased last year.
